annotations.title: NSW, Queensland, WA and SA rents by postcode, suburb or locality

description: Median weekly rent of new bonds lodged in the latest quarter, all dwellings together, with the bond count and the change on a year before, for one state per call: NSW by postcode or council (NSW Department of Communities and Justice), QLD by suburb or council (Residential Tenancies Authority), WA by locality (calculated by DwellDelta from the Government of Western Australia's bond records), SA by suburb (SA Housing Trust, Private Rent Report; one quarter held, so no change on a year; its publisher's page states no licence, the catalogues list CC BY). Each file states CC BY 4.0. area or council names the place the question is about; with neither, the answer is the state's own figure. The figures are new-bond medians, not advertised rents. Each state measures in its own way, so the states are not one series: their figures cannot be added together or compared as one. Each answer states its quarter, its source line and the source's limits. Victoria is in vic_rents. For NSW and QLD, dwelling_type or bedrooms (or both) give the publisher's figure for that kind of home instead - a two-bedroom unit, a three-bedroom house. Only combinations the publisher reports are answered: one with no published median is said to have none, and neither another area's figure nor the all-dwellings figure stands in for it. Many such figures rest on few bonds. WA and SA have no figures by dwelling type or bedrooms. For questions such as "median rent in Parramatta".

area.description: NSW: a postcode, or a suburb (answered for its whole postcode). QLD: a suburb. WA: a locality. SA: a suburb. Part of a suburb or locality name works

bedrooms.description: NSW and QLD only: a number of bedrooms, as '2' or '2 bedrooms'. NSW also has Bedsitter, and 4 means DCJ's '4 or more Bedrooms'; a number above 4 is answered under that label too, and the answer says it is not for that number alone. QLD: the RTA publishes flats of 1 to 3, houses of 2 to 4 and town houses of 2 to 3, and does not define its labels - reading the number as bedrooms is DwellDelta's. A plus means 'or more', which only DCJ's 4 has: '3+', and any 'N+' for QLD, is refused, not answered as exactly N. Without dwelling_type, every type the publisher reports at that size is given

council.description: A council (NSW or QLD), or part of its name

dwelling_type.description: NSW and QLD only. NSW (DCJ's labels): House, Townhouse, Flat/Unit, Other. QLD (the RTA's): Flat, House, Townhouse. 'unit' and 'apartment' are read as flat/unit. Without bedrooms, every size the publisher reports for that type is given

state.description: NSW, QLD, WA or SA - one state per call
